Stated Claim / Post Context:
Albanese’s United Nations climate hypocrisy

Actual Article Body:
The Prime Minister delivered a sort of homily to the United Nations, saying Australia “understands the dangers of global warming and the urgency of climate action”. But his actions belie his words, argues Pip Hinman.

Anthony Albanese’s speech to the United Nations during “climate week” revealed just how out of touch he and his government are with the widespread community concern over runaway climate change.

He said scientists have “warned” us about climate change and that Australia “understands the dangers of global warming and the urgency of climate action”.

He went on to praise firefighters and special emergency service workers for showing the “best of humanity” in the 2019–20 Black Summer bushfire crisis and various devastating floods.

With hand on heart, Albanese said: “There’s no avoiding the scale of our responsibility — or the cost of inaction”, before praising Australians for “choosing to electrify” with “clean, reliable, more affordable energy”.

Higher-Page Jacobian and Albanese Tori

We construct, through Hodge-theoretical methods, what we call the $E_r$-Jacobian torus, the $E_r$-Albanese torus and the $E_r$-Albanese map of any compact complex manifold that is either {\it page-(r-1)-$\partial\bar\partial$} or {\it $E_r$-sGG}. These two classes of manifolds, the former of which is contained in the latter, have been introduced recently by both authors jointly with J. Stelzig, respectively by the first-named author. A Hodge theory is also developed for the latter class of manifolds. We then apply our results to give structure theorems and an identity of algebraic dimensions in terms of the $E_r$-Albanese map and torus.
